ADMIN WORKSPACE

The governance path, end to end

Every card is a link. The three colours are the three layers that must never be confused: blue is an agent step, purple is a human step, teal is publication.

THE RECORD
Overview
queues & status

who/what/when/hash
Publication history
every publish
The one rule this workspace exists to hold

An automated check never supplies human sign-off. The schema validator, the machine correctness check and the AI reviewer are all agent steps — blue throughout. They inform a person; they never approve. Human approval is a named reviewer signing one immutable revision, bound to its content hash. Publication makes that exact approved revision live, and refuses if the approval does not match the current hash. In report mode the gate records what it would block but still serves; only enforce mode makes human approval a precondition to serving. Every name, hash and date is illustrative sample data.

The three layers, never interchangeable
Agent review

Schema validation, machine correctness, originality, the AI reviewer. Blue. Informs; never approves.

Human approval

A named person signs one immutable revision, bound to its content hash. Purple. The only sign-off.

Published

The approved revision goes live, if its hash still matches. Teal. Separate, later, reversible.

Claims this design deliberately does not make
That a passing check is an approval. Agents inform; a person signs off.
That an approval covers “the question”. It covers one revision hash, and goes stale when the content changes.
That report-mode content is human-verified. The dashboard states how many of the served questions actually carry an approval.
A person’s name on an automated step. The actor is “System” for agent actions.
A child’s identity or free text in Support. Reports are a question id, a year and a fixed reason.

title: Reference · Decisions
text:
ADMIN WORKSPACE

Proposed decisions

Ten positions. Four are already the product’s behaviour, four are recommendations, two are builds. D4 is the one that decides whether the governance this workspace shows is actually enforced.

#	POSITION	STATUS	WHY, AND WHAT TURNS ON IT
D1	Agent review, human approval and publication are three states
Shown in three colours, never merged. A status is always one of the three, explicitly.
	RECOMMENDED	The data model already separates governance (automated), findings (AI reviewer) and approval (approvedBy/approvedAt). The UI must not collapse them, because collapsing them is exactly how un-reviewed content reaches children.
D2	Approval binds to an immutable revision hash
The reviewer, the revision number and the content hash are recorded together; a changed revision needs a new approval.
	BUILT ALREADY	ValidatedApprovalTarget carries revision + contentHash, item_versions are immutable whole-row, and findings carry matchesCurrentRevision. The stale-revision block is enforced, not advisory.
D3	A passing check never approves
Machine checks and the AI reviewer are drawn as information for a person, never as a sign-off, and publication refuses without a human approval.
	RECOMMENDED	The single most important honesty rule in the whole product. It is why the publication block "no human approval" is drawn as the common case.
D4	Report vs enforce is shown honestly
The dashboard states that report-mode programmes serve un-approved content, and how many served questions carry an approval.
	NEEDS SIGN-OFF	PROGRAMME_PUBLICATION_MODES is empty, so every programme is report except scholarship/edutest. 96.7% of served questions carry no approval. Moving NAPLAN/ICAS to enforce is a product and operational decision.
D5	Unpublish and reject are destructive, and confirmed
Both warn, state what is kept, and are logged against a name.
	RECOMMENDED	Taking a question out of service changes what children see immediately; it needs a deliberate confirmation.
D6	Support shows the question, not the child
Reports carry an id, a year and a fixed reason. No child name, answers or free text.
	BUILT ALREADY	The report form collects fixed reasons and no child free text, so there is nothing sensitive to surface. Account issues are handled without opening a child record.
D7	A reviewer / senior-reviewer split
Drawn in the permission-denied state: approving some programmes needs a higher role.
	NEEDS A BUILD	Roles today are student/parent/teacher/admin. Per-programme approval rights and a reviewer tier are a build. The design states the boundary rather than hiding controls.
D8	Writing marks are claimed only after the server confirms
The child reads "not yet marked" until the mark is saved; confirming records the marker.
	BUILT ALREADY	Manual marks already go through get_manual_review_response / pending_manual. Same honesty rule as the student results screens.
D9	The activity log names System for automated steps
No person is ever the actor on an agent action.
	RECOMMENDED	An audit trail that attributes a machine step to a person is worse than none; it launders automation as human judgement.
D10	A soft lock for concurrent review
Drawn as "someone else is reviewing this now".
	NEEDS A BUILD	Needs a presence signal. The hard guarantee without it is the stale-revision block plus idempotent approval of an unchanged revision.

title: Reference · Dependencies
text:
ADMIN WORKSPACE

Backend dependencies

Checked against origin/dev on 8 November 2026. The governance data model is unusually complete; what is mostly missing is the reviewer-facing UI this canvas designs, plus roles and a few presence/escalation signals.

Already in the repository
BUILT ALREADY
WHAT	WHERE	WHAT IT GIVES THE DESIGN
The review record	admin-review/contracts	ReviewEntry: source + contentHash + revision, governance (automated gate), findings (AI reviewer, with matchesCurrentRevision), approval (approvedBy/approvedAt). The whole three-layer model.
Approval, revision-bound	content-governance/approval-verification	ValidatedApprovalTarget (revision + contentHash), ApprovalDecision (approve/reject/revise), human publication + writing-prompt approval schemas, verifyApprovalRecord.
Gate modes	content-governance/gate-config	report vs enforce per programme; scholarship/edutest enforce, the rest report. Drives the honest publication status.
Publication integrity	content-governance/publication-integrity	Content-hash checks that back the stale-approval block.
Immutable revisions	item_versions (migration)	Whole-row immutability, so a revision hash is a stable thing to bind an approval to.
Writing marks	/api/teacher/marking, get_manual_review_response	Rubric + feedback + pending_manual. The writing-review screen.
An admin shell	admin-analytics/AdminShell	A real sidebar shell with sections (Draft review, Analytics, Operations, Intelligence) and a mobile nav.
Erasure / support plumbing	erasure_requests, erasure_processor (migrations)	The account-side of support rests on real, audited request handling.
Has to be built
NEEDS A BUILD
The reviewer-facing review and approval UI this canvas designs. The data and the schemas exist; the human workflow over them is what is new.
A reviewer / senior-reviewer role and per-programme approval rights. Roles today are student/parent/teacher/admin.
Presence & escalation signals: a soft lock for concurrent review, and the routing for a “something upset me” report.
Marker-facing redaction on writing responses beyond year level.
A unified activity log view across approvals, publications and marks (the records exist in places; the single audit view is new).
Needs a decision from outside design
NEEDS SIGN-OFF
Which programmes move from report to enforce, and when. Until NAPLAN/ICAS enforce, human approval is recorded but not required to serve — the 96.7%-unapproved reality. This is the decision that makes the whole workspace matter.
The escalation policy for a child’s distress report: who is notified, how fast, and what is auto-pulled.
Who may be a reviewer, and whether approval of children’s content needs a named, accountable individual by policy.
